story_type: spacewalk repair: astronauts cut loose a jammed solar wing with improvised tools, 1973
hook: Power running out. The fix was outside, with nothing to hold.
narration: Two astronauts went outside to cut loose a stuck solar wing, with almost nothing to hold on to.
Skylab's big solar wing had been jammed since launch, pinned by pieces of its own torn shield.
By the fifth day, some batteries were failing and the power shortage turned critical.
In an underwater simulator in Alabama, the backup crew worked out a plan using only tools like the ones aboard.
On June seventh, 1973, Pete Conrad and Joe Kerwin went out.
They joined sunshade poles into a handrail, anchored by a pair of cutters hooked onto the strap that held the wing.
In weightlessness, every pull pushes you back the other way, so each move needs something solid to brace against.
[short pause] Conrad clipped a tether to the wing. The cutters bit through the strap, and they pulled.
outcome: The wing swung fully open, and within hours Skylab's electrical power nearly doubled.
title: Spacewalk to free a jammed solar wing
description:
On June 7, 1973, Skylab astronauts Pete Conrad and Joe Kerwin spacewalked to free the station's jammed solar wing, using sunshade poles and a cable cutter. Within hours Skylab's power almost doubled. From the 1973 NASA film Skylab: The First 40 Days.
